copy.dek: Week 7 brings a crowded 4-2 pack, a Giggle Island date with a Hebrew Hammer who has been hot, and Paul facing the one opponent who never has a bad week. Reid's roster is also running low on healthy receivers.
preview_intro: Six teams sit at 4-2, and the five-team pile behind them at 3-3 is close enough to jump the line with one good Sunday. Paul leads the power rankings at 52-20 all-play with a 131.35 scoring average, and he has two losses to show for it. This week he takes on The Median, who wins nothing but never loses by accident either.

Elsewhere the bottom is getting crowded. Tex and Eamonn are both 1-5, Ian is 2-4, and every one of them is one result away from a decent week or a long month. Injuries are doing real damage too: Reid has a RB out and a WR projected at zero, and Eamonn is missing DJ Moore. Here's the full slate.

game_of_week.blurb: Andy's Giggle Island is second in the power rankings at 49-23 all-play and projects at 101.19. Medvene's Hebrew Hammer is 3-3 and projects at 74.39, but the Hammer posted 139.9 and 152.4 in Weeks 4 and 5 before a 91.3 dud last week. If that high-scoring version of the Hammer shows up, Andy's projected cushion disappears fast.

upcoming.blurb: Tex is 1-5 and has lost two straight, though his 28-44 all-play record says he has been unluckier than he looks. Daniel's Flutes are 4-2 but have fallen to 100.6 after a 172.2 in Week 3. The projection favors the Flutes 99.43 to 90.72, and neither side lists an injured starter.

Nick's Murder Hornets are 4-2 with two straight wins, but they have the better record only on paper. Costa projects at 108.54 against Nick's 97.11 and is coming off a 127.9 that included Kenneth Walker's 28. No injured starters on either side, so this one comes down to scoring.

Greg's Kimballs are 4th in the power rankings but 3-3 after losing two straight, including an 80.4 last week. Ian is 2-4 and projects at 98.02 against Greg's 82.29, so the home underdog is the favorite here. T.J. Hockenson is questionable at TE for Ian.

Eamonn is 1-5 and has lost four straight, and he is without DJ Moore (OUT), which does not help a team averaging 97.97. Joe's Bible Bonkers took the Week 6 top score with 133.3 and projects at 76.81, a slim edge over Eamonn's 71.94. A.J. Brown is questionable for Joe, so watch his status.

This is the matchup of two 4-2 teams that are both banged up. George's Baby Dolls have won three straight on a 9th-ranked power profile, and Tyler Warren (TE) is OUT. Reid projects at 78.82 to George's 65.01 despite Quinshon Judkins OUT, Mike Evans questionable and Terry McLaurin doubtful and projected at zero.

Paul gets The Median, which scores the league median every week and projects to nothing in particular. Paul's 131.35 average is far above last week's 101.9 median, so he should clear it. Romeo Doubs is on injury reserve but is still listed in Paul's lineup, so he deserves a look before kickoff.
Andy is the favorite at 101.19 to 74.39 and has won two straight. Medvene is 3-3 and coming off a 91.3 loss to The Median, so he is looking for a rebound. Neither team has an injured starter.

copy.power: Paul is on top at 52-20 all-play and has only 4-2 to show for it, with Andy and Daniel close behind. George is the luckiest team in the league at +1.4, a 4-2 record on a 9th-ranked all-play résumé, while Nick (+0.8) and Reid (+0.7) are also doing better than their scores suggest. Tex is the unluckiest at -1.3, a 1-5 team with the 11th-best all-play mark, ahead of Greg (-0.5) and Eamonn (-0.5).
copy.injury_spotlight: Reid's Training Room is busy. Quinshon Judkins (RB) is OUT, Mike Evans (WR) is questionable, and Terry McLaurin (WR) is doubtful and projected at 0.0, so he is a starter producing nothing. Breece Hall is also OUT on IR. Last week McLaurin's 2.5 stayed in the lineup while DK Metcalf's 15.5 sat on the bench, so the receiver room needs attention before George and his 65.01 projection arrive.
copy.playoffs: It is far too early to draw lines, but six teams are in the top group right now: Paul, Andy, Daniel, Reid, Nick and George, all 4-2. Greg and Costa are knocking at 3-3. Joe, Medvene, Ian, Tex and Eamonn are the long shots, with Tex and Eamonn at 1-5. A lot can change in eight weeks, and with this many teams bunched together, a single week can reshuffle the order.
recap: Joe's Bible Bonkers took the weekly top prize with 133.3 and beat Paul's 120.9, a score that would have won most weeks. Costa's 127.9 was the next-best total, and Kenneth Walker's 28.0 helped him beat Eamonn by 55.6. Eamonn's 72.3 was the week's low. Nick held off Daniel by 9.0 and George won with only 96.9, thanks to Trevor Lawrence's 28.4.

The week's other bad scores came from Reid (77.9, a loss to Andy) and Greg (80.4). Reid's lineup left DK Metcalf's 15.5 on the bench for Terry McLaurin's 2.5. Medvene's 91.3 lost to The Median's 101.9.

results.blurb: Nick's Murder Hornets edged the Flutes 109.6 to 100.6, led by James Cook III's 22.5. Daniel's Steelers D/ST scored 19.7 and still was not enough.
Ian beat Tex 114.4 to 101.9, with Tre Tucker's 24.5 from the flex spot against a 7.95 projection. Kyle Pitts scored 20.5 for Tex, but the loss was his second in a row.
Costa won 127.9 to 72.3, the week's biggest blowout. Kenneth Walker's 28.0 did a lot of it, and even Drake Maye's 25.8 could not help Eamonn.
George beat Greg 96.9 to 80.4 with Trevor Lawrence's 28.4 doing the heavy lifting. Chris Olave's 13.0 led Greg's side, and the Kimballs have now lost two straight.
Joe beat Paul 133.3 to 120.9 and took the week's top score. Josh Allen scored 21.6 against a 27.29 projection, and Paul's 120.9 was the highest score in a loss this week.
Andy's Giggle Island beat Reid 111.9 to 77.9 behind Christian McCaffrey's 26.5. Caleb Williams scored 21.8 for Reid, but not much else worked.
Medvene lost to The Median 101.9 to 91.3, even with Jayden Daniels scoring 24.6. The Median did nothing and still beat him.

teams.blurb: Paul is first in the power rankings with 788.1 points and a 5-1 mark against the median, yet he is only 4-2. Two weeks over 140 came with bad luck attached (-0.3).
Andy is 4-2 with two straight wins and the second-best all-play record. His 88.5 in Week 4 is the only blemish on a strong scoring run.
Daniel is 4-2 but has scored 114.4, 112.6 and 100.6 in his last three, down from a 172.2 peak in Week 3. His power rank of 3 depends on getting some of that scoring back.
Reid is 4-2 and 5th in power, helped by a +0.7 luck rating, but a 77.9 last week and a thin injury report have him on a two-game slide in scoring. Watch his lineup choices.
Nick is 4-2 with two straight wins, a 111.78 average and a +0.8 luck rating. He has not scored over 127.5 all season, so he is winning on consistency.
George is 4-2 on three straight wins, but he is 1-4 against the median and has the second-luckiest record in the league at +1.4. His 160.4 in Week 1 is a long way from his 96.9 last week.
Greg is 3-3 with 737.4 points, fourth in power and fourth in all-play. He has lost two straight, though, and his 80.4 last week was far below his 122.9 average.
Costa is 3-3 and 7th in power with a 110.85 average. His 127.9 last week was the second-best score in the league.
Joe is 3-3 after a 133.3 that won the week, and it is his best score by a wide margin. The rest of his scores sit between 98.6 and 106.8, so he needs to prove last week was not a one-off.
Medvene is 3-3 and had back-to-back scores of 139.9 and 152.4, then fell to 91.3 and a loss to The Median. He is the most volatile roster in the league.
Ian is 2-4 with a 168.8 in Week 2 and not much else above 114.4. He has won one in a row and ranks 12th in power.
Tex is 1-5 but has scored 107.15 on average, so the record is worse than the team. His -1.3 luck rating is the league's lowest.
Eamonn is 1-5 with four straight losses and the league's lowest average at 97.97. With DJ Moore out, things look rough.

awards.quip: Joe's 133.3 was the week's top score and takes the payout, a nice change of pace for the Bible Bonkers.
Eamonn's 72.3 was the week's low, and Drake Maye's 25.8 was the only good part.
Costa beat Eamonn by 55.6, the biggest margin of the week.
Nick survived the Flutes by 9.0, which is the closest anyone came to a nail-biter.
George won with just 96.9, which is the sort of score that usually loses.
Paul scored 120.9 and lost, because Joe had a better week.
Trevor Lawrence scored 28.4 for George, against a projection of 18.75.
Reid left DK Metcalf's 15.5 on the bench and started Terry McLaurin's 2.5, a 13.0-point gap.

round_up: The league is bunched together. Six teams are at 4-2, five are at 3-3, and the all-play standings suggest Paul, Andy and Daniel are the strongest of the group, with the rest more dependent on schedule luck.
Luck is shaping the table. George and Nick are winning more than their scoring says they should, while Tex is 1-5 with a scoring average of 107.15, which is nearly the same as Joe's and Medvene's.
The injury list is a problem to track. Reid has multiple receivers and running backs dinged, Eamonn is missing DJ Moore, and Joe, George and Ian each have a starter to watch before kickoff.
Watch Paul against The Median, Andy against Medvene, and whether Joe's big week was a fluke. If Eamonn can't beat Joe, the bottom of the table starts to look settled.
